earlier_scan.note: Only Voorhoeve 1970 comparative/subclassification notes on Waruna; no grammar or phonology located.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 345-459. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.345
sources.note: p.353: 'The only source of information on Waruna is a word list published by Riley (and Ray) (1930-31).' p.355 sec. 2.6.2.2.1.2.2 Waruna: would rather classify it as a dialect of Gogodala; 'a definite assessment will have to wait till more data has become available.' Stress statements given only for Suki (p.352, generally first syllable) and Gogodala (p.354, 'stress is phonemic'); none for Waruna.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2020-2024. Suki-Aramia River; Waruna. NewGuineaWorld (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch).
sources.note: Sources section: Waruna data = 'Riley and Ray (1930-1931: 172-189) 534 comparative terms' only; the Waruna language page is empty; historical phonology of segments only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Reesink, Ger P. 1976. Languages of the Aramia River area. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 19, Pacific Linguistics A-45: 1-37. doi:10.15144/PL-A45.1
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'Notes on phonology and grammar' (pp.9-10) gives a tentative phoneme inventory for Ari, which 'could well be identified with Waruna' (~50% identical words with Riley's Waruna list); no statement on stress for Ari or Waruna.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1970. Some notes on the Suki-Gogodala subgroup of the Central and South New Guinea Phylum. In Wurm & Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, PL C-13: 1245-1270.
sources.note: Treats Suki and Gogodala only (appendix 'Accent' for each); Waruna is not discussed at all.

sources.citation: Riley, E. Baxter & Sidney H. Ray. 1931. Sixteen vocabularies from the Fly River, Papua [part 3, incl. S.H. Ray, 'Notes on the Vocabularies. A. Sounds']. Anthropos 26: 171-192.
sources.note: p.191 (pdf p.207): 'In Gogodara, Adiba and Waruna the sounds are as in Kiwai with the addition of gw... Waruna has l in the word kalima blood, which is... possibly a mistake.' Segment list only; nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the notes.

sources.citation: Riley, E. Baxter & Sidney H. Ray. 1930. Sixteen vocabularies from the Fly River, Papua [parts 1-2]. Anthropos 25: 173-193, 831-850.
sources.note: p.174 no.16 locates Waruna ('on the western border of the Gogodara region, inland from the north shore of the Fly'); comparative wordlist columns only; nothing on stress (part 2 read as archive.org scanned text).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1923. The languages of the Western Division of Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 53: 332-360.
sources.note: p.336 lists Waruna as a village/language of the Gogodara group; classification and comparative vocabulary; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Neuendorf, A.K. n.d. Gogodala grammar (with phonemic statement). Unpublished ms., Asia Pacific Christian Mission, 99 pp. (Glottolog ref 551064).

sources.note: Voorhoeve 1975 regards Waruna as possibly a Gogodala dialect; Neuendorf's phonemic statement is the fullest description of the nearest variety and would be the proxy if Waruna is catalogued under Gogodala. Not a Waruna source.
